title: RNNs & LSTM cells
summary: Recurrence carries a hidden state through time; the LSTM adds a gated cell state.
why: The cell-state path gives gradients an additive route through long sequences.
interview: Derive the gate equations and identify when the gradient highway still decays.
derivation: A vanilla RNN gradient contains products of recurrent Jacobians, including W_hh transpose and activation derivatives. Repeated singular values below or above one produce decay or explosion.
The direct cell path derivative contains products of forget gates. Gates near one help preserve gradients, but LSTMs do not eliminate all vanishing gradients.

steps.note: Sequence dependency prevents full time-step parallelism.
One fused matrix multiply can produce 4H activations.
Additive path combines retained and written content.
Both h and c must be carried to the next step.

traps: Forgetting to detach carried states grows the autograd graph across batches.
Padding needs packing or a mask so it does not overwrite valid states.
Gradient clipping handles explosions, not missing long-range signal.
tradeoff: Recurrence has compact persistent state but serial time dependence limits training parallelism.
code:
import torch
from torch import nn

cell = nn.LSTMCell(16, 32)
h = torch.zeros(2, 32)
c = torch.zeros_like(h)
for x in torch.randn(5, 2, 16):
    h, c = cell(x, (h, c))
assert h.shape == c.shape == (2, 32)

variants.title: Cell-state highway
variants.flow:
c[t-1] -- multiply f -- add (i * candidate) --> c[t]
c[t] -- tanh -- multiply o --> h[t]
variants.detail: Forget, input, candidate, and output branches are computed from x[t] and h[t-1].

explanations.title: Unroll the recurrence before reasoning about gradients
paragraphs: A vanilla RNN reads x_t [B,Din] and h_(t-1) [B,Dh], then produces h_t [B,Dh]. The same recurrent parameters are reused at every time step. Sequence classification may consume the last valid state; token labeling consumes all states.

Backpropagation through time multiplies recurrent Jacobians. tanh derivatives are at most one, while the recurrent matrix can contract or amplify directions. Repeated products can make early-token gradients vanish or explode. Gradient clipping controls large gradients but does not restore vanished ones.

Padded batches need lengths or masks. Reading the final padded state as the sentence representation changes the computation. A bidirectional RNN reads future context and is unsuitable for strictly causal online generation without changing the task.

explanations.title: Four gates and the cell-state path
paragraphs: Concatenate x_t and h_(t-1), then project to four Dh-wide vectors. Sigmoid produces forget f_t, input i_t, and output o_t gates in [0,1]. tanh produces the candidate g_t. The cell update adds retained memory and new content.

The direct path through cell state multiplies by f_t rather than a full recurrent matrix at every step. Forget gates near one can preserve a gradient over many steps. Indirect paths still exist through the gates and hidden states, so LSTMs do not guarantee perfect memory.

Both c_t and h_t must be carried between chunks for stateful inference. Truncated backprop detaches the state at chunk boundaries to limit the graph; it intentionally removes gradient paths across those boundaries.

explanations.title: Trace a single cell coordinate
paragraphs: Suppose c_prev=2, f=0.9, i=0.2, candidate=0.5, and o=0.8. The new cell is 0.9*2 + 0.2*0.5 = 1.9. The visible hidden coordinate is 0.8*tanh(1.9), approximately 0.765. Cell memory and exposed hidden state serve different roles.

Recurrence is sequential along time even when gates within a step are matrix products. Transformers parallelize training token positions at the cost of attention work; RNN inference carries a fixed-size state but may compress away information needed much later.
